title: USPS Carries Nearly Half Its Peak Mail, Yet Stamps Cost More
hook: Fewer letters made mailing one more expensive, not cheaper.
closing: A nationwide postal network gets harder to fund as every mailbox receives less mail.
question: What do you still mail?

segments.say: USPS mail fell to 109 billion pieces, leaving the network with nearly half its former traffic.
USPS First-Class Mail fell to 46 billion pieces, showing personal and business letters disappeared fastest.
A USPS stamp reached 68 cents, so shrinking volume did not make sending a letter cheaper.
